review.summary: I reviewed only the supplied text for revision 58180fc4: the legacy `clientIp` and `checkRateLimit` code, plus the call sites in the portal access, voucher redeem, referral and live-admission routes. Nothing I found is a BLOCKER or MAJOR. Every call site still uses the same `checkRateLimit(request, key, limit, windowMs)` signature, and each returns early when `limited` is set. The one exception is the referral route, which deliberately redirects to `/billing/plans` instead. Upstash and memory provider errors fail closed with `serviceUnavailable()`. The legacy `clientIp` trusted the client-supplied `cf-connecting-ip` and `x-forwarded-for` headers, which callers can fake. As stated, the patch replaces that with `request.ip` from the adapter, and there are no source changes since the prior review. Scope limitation: the post-patch IP-resolution source wasn't in this text, so this review relies on the prior review of the same revision for that code. That limitation does not block LOCAL patch acceptance. The remaining items are documented MINOR and NIT residuals about deployment and configuration. This review does not certify cloud deployment, which is still unapproved, overall work-package readiness, test results or release.

findings.area: runtime provider path (memory / upstash_redis) client identity
findings.issue: Runtime rate-limit mode only works when the hosting adapter supplies `request.ip`. Running ordinary `next dev` or `next start` in runtime mode is unsupported. This is a documented residual risk, not part of the shipping configuration.
findings.evidence: The legacy `clientIp` fell back from `cf-connecting-ip` to `x-forwarded-for` to "unknown". Callers can set those headers themselves, and every caller without them shared one "unknown" bucket. The task says the patched path relies on the adapter's `request.ip` and that the tested local deployment uses the proof-backed `cloudflare_waf` provider.
findings.impact: If runtime mode is ever turned on where `request.ip` is missing, requests either fail closed (503) or share one bucket. Either way, access, voucher, referral and live-admission availability would suffer. This does not affect the tested cloudflare configuration.
findings.recommended_fix: Keep this documented as unsupported. Also add a startup or config guard that rejects the memory and upstash providers when the runtime cannot supply `request.ip`.
findings.required_test: Unit test: with the memory provider and no `request.ip`, check that `checkRateLimit` never reads `cf-connecting-ip` or `x-forwarded-for` and that its fail-closed or rejection behavior is deterministic.

findings.area: `cloudflare_waf` early return; proof header shared by the entry and live-chat paths
findings.issue: Under `cloudflare_waf`, `checkRateLimit` returns null with no checks inside the app. All enforcement, including separate per-key counting, therefore depends on edge rules. The proof header also needs the same injected value on the entry and live-chat paths when the edge injects one global value. Using different values requires path-specific edge injection.
findings.evidence: `if (provider === "cloudflare_waf") return null;`. The call sites use separate keys and limits: portal access preview at 60 and confirm at 30, voucher redeem at 60 and confirm at 30, referral entry at 60, and live-admission and live-admission-release at 120 each. The route comment says DELETE requests must have their own count so they can't use up the admission quota.
findings.impact: If the edge rules don't match each path, method and limit, the app enforces nothing. For example, a single shared WAF rule would let a flood of DELETE requests to live-admission use up the admission quota. A mismatched proof-header value would break either entry or live-chat requests.
findings.recommended_fix: In the deployment runbook, list the required WAF rules for each path and method, with limits matching the keys above. Also state the rule for injecting the proof header: one global value, or path-specific values.
findings.required_test: Deployment checklist and edge smoke test: confirm separate counting for POST and DELETE on live-admission, and confirm the proof header is accepted on both the entry and live-chat paths. This applies to cloud deployment, which stays unapproved and outside this local acceptance.

findings.issue: The claim that a test covers provider ordering is kept as a residual and hasn't been independently verified here. The implementation order itself is visible in the code.
findings.evidence: The code checks `cloudflare_waf` first and returns early, then chooses `upstash_redis` or memory inside a try/catch that falls back to `serviceUnavailable()`.
findings.impact: This only affects how well regressions are caught. Runtime behavior is unaffected.
findings.recommended_fix: Add or point to a test that checks provider selection order and that provider errors fail closed.
findings.required_test: Parameterized test over each provider ID, including a provider that throws, checking that the result is null, 429 or 503 as expected.
